answer: Operator-Linked Resource Ledger. Each new identity must draw compute and bandwidth from a hardware root tied to a verified operator account, logged like cargo moving along a wharf. An operator whose identities exceed a churn threshold on any river of activity (registration, messaging, transactions) loses shared throughput quota across all its identities at once. The attacker pays by sacrificing the throughput of every agent it controls, not one wallet: adding a sybil costs the operator a basalt-hard, proportional cut to its entire fleet's capacity.
